title: U.S. Senate · South Carolina

context.text: This election fills the Class II Senate seat formerly held by Lindsey Graham (R), who won renomination in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary and died on July 11, 2026. Gov. Henry McMaster appointed Graham's sister, Darline Graham, to the seat on July 13, 2026. A special Republican primary (August 11) and runoff (August 25) were held to select the party's replacement nominee; Darline Graham won that runoff and appears on the November 3 general-election ballot.
Annie Andrews won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026 with 61.5% of the vote, defeating Brandon Brown and Kyle Freeman.
Kasie Whitener won the Libertarian Party's nominating convention on April 11, 2026.

candidates.name: Darline Graham
candidates.ballotNote: Won the special Republican primary runoff (Aug. 25, 2026) to become the general-election nominee after Lindsey Graham's death

summary.text: Darline Graham was appointed to the U.S. Senate by Gov. Henry McMaster on July 13, 2026 to succeed her brother, Lindsey Graham, who died in office. She is running to complete the remainder of the term.

background.text: Born in Central, South Carolina. Earned a bachelor's degree from the College of Charleston (1989) and a graduate degree from South Carolina State University (2009).
Worked as a vocational rehabilitation counselor, served as a commissioner with the South Carolina Commission for the Blind, and worked with the South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, issue statements, or Candidate Connection survey response found for Darline Graham as of research date; she has held office only since July 2026. Background is from Ballotpedia's biographical summary.

candidates.name: Annie Andrews
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 61.5% of the vote

summary.text: Annie Andrews is a pediatrician running for U.S. Senate as the Democratic nominee.

positions.summary: Campaign platform lists advocating a public option and protecting and expanding Medicaid and Medicare among her Senate goals.
positions.quote: Protect and expand Medicaid and Medicare

positions.summary: Campaign platform says she will fight to restore the protections of Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Restore the protections of Roe v. Wade

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for universal background checks, banning "weapons of war," and safe storage laws.
Campaign platform says she will fight to end tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy and corporate polluters.
positions.quote: End tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy and corporate polluters

positions.summary: Campaign platform says she will fight to require Congress to approve use of military force.
positions.quote: Require Congress to approve use of military force

researchNotes: Basic-tier research. Darline Graham was appointed to this seat in July 2026 after Lindsey Graham's death; her federal key-vote and FEC data (if added later by script) will reflect only her short tenure. This slate and the Graham appointment/death were independently confirmed against Wikipedia, CBS News, and the official senate.gov senator roster (which lists 'Graham, Darline' for South Carolina, Class II), since the sole cited source was Ballotpedia. Andrews's summary originally called her a 'Charleston pediatrician' citing only her Ballotpedia page, which does not state her profession; corrected to cite her campaign website, which confirms she is a pediatrician (no independent confirmation that she practices in Charleston specifically, so that detail was dropped). Several independent candidates on the ballot have no discoverable public record beyond their ballot listing; a Democratic write-in candidate (Catherine Fleming Bruce) is not included per the write-in exclusion in the research standard's ballot scope.
